Plot pathways as a heatmap of next-state probabilities

Source: R/plot_pathways.R
plot_pathways.Rd

plot_pathways() draws the pathway table of a context tree as a heatmap: one row per pathway, one column per next state, and the fitted probability \(P(\mathrm{next} \mid \mathrm{pathway})\) as fill. The pathway table lists, for every history, how often it occurs and what tends to follow it. The most likely next state of each row is printed in bold, other probabilities of at least 0.05 in plain text, and pathways whose most likely next state differs from that of their shorter suffix are marked with a leading >. One display then shows which pathways are common, which lead almost always to one state, which leave the next state open, and where a longer history changes the prediction that a first-order model would make.

Rows are the top pathways by count, by divergence from the shorter suffix, or by depth (the root is not shown). For the full distribution of a few contexts as bar charts use plot_distributions(); to rank pathways by how much their history matters use plot_divergence().

Usage

plot_pathways(
  tree,
  top = 20L,
  sort_by = c("count", "divergence", "depth"),
  min_count = 5L,
  show_flips = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

top

Maximum number of pathways shown. Default 20.

sort_by

Order of the rows: "count" (default), "divergence" or "depth" (deepest first).

min_count

Pathways with a lower count are dropped. Default 5.

show_flips

Mark pathways whose most likely next state differs from their parent's. Default TRUE.

title

Plot title. Default NULL: a title naming the ordering.

...

Ignored.

Value

A ggplot object: a heatmap of pathways by next states.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) tree is not a transitiontrees object.

transitiontrees_empty_result

(error) no pathway reaches min_count.

See also

tree_pathways() for the table; plot_distributions(), plot_divergence().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
plot_pathways(tree, top = 12)

plot_pathways(tree, sort_by = "divergence", top = 12)
